cmd_misc_cache_entries: Second line of `atlas cache status`: how many entries the task cache holds and its size against the cap.
cmd_misc_cache_freed: Result of `atlas cache gc` and `atlas cache clear`, after the command name and a colon; {size} is a size such as 12.5 MiB.
cmd_misc_cache_totals: Line of `atlas cache status` (the total, then one per project after the project name): cache hits and misses, and the time hits saved.
cmd_misc_config_ports: Heading of the service port list printed by `atlas config check` when the project has a port offset; {offset} is the number added to each port.
cmd_misc_config_valid: Output of `atlas config check` when atlas.yaml has no errors; {path} is the file.
cmd_misc_dc_app_mismatch: Detail of the desktop-app check when the app's version differs from the CLI's; {version} may be dc_unknown_version.
cmd_misc_dc_app_missing: Detail of the desktop-app check on a machine with a graphical session and no app.
cmd_misc_dc_app_none: Detail of the desktop-app check on a machine with no graphical session, which is fine.

cmd_misc_dc_app_ok.description: Detail of the desktop-app check when it passes: where it is and its version.

cmd_misc_dc_atlas_elsewhere: Detail of the new-terminal check when another `atlas` comes first on PATH.
cmd_misc_dc_atlas_elsewhere_fix: Fix of the new-terminal check when another `atlas` comes first on PATH.
cmd_misc_dc_atlas_found: Detail of the new-terminal check when it passes: the path a new terminal resolves `atlas` to.
cmd_misc_dc_atlas_missing: Detail of the new-terminal check when it fails (the case behind issue #265).
cmd_misc_dc_atlas_missing_fix: Fix of the new-terminal check when it fails; {command} is the curl line of the installer.
cmd_misc_dc_fix_label: Label before the command or step that fixes a failing check in `atlas doctor`, under the check's label.

cmd_misc_dc_host_ok.description: Detail of the terminal-host check when hostd answers the handshake.
cmd_misc_dc_host_ok.distinct: state word of a check row

cmd_misc_dc_host_silent: Detail of the terminal-host check when hostd does not answer; {why} is the cause.

cmd_misc_dc_name_desktop_app.description: Label of the third check of `atlas doctor`: Atlas Desktop installed and on the CLI's version.

cmd_misc_dc_name_new_terminal.description: Label of the first check of `atlas doctor`: does a new terminal find `atlas`.

cmd_misc_dc_name_terminal_host.description: Label of the fourth check of `atlas doctor`: does hostd answer.

cmd_misc_dc_name_this_terminal.description: Label of the second check of `atlas doctor`: is the install folder on this shell's PATH.

cmd_misc_dc_path_missing: Detail of the this-terminal check when the install folder is not on PATH.
cmd_misc_dc_path_ok: Detail of the this-terminal check when it passes.
cmd_misc_dc_probe_failed: Detail of the new-terminal check when the probe failed; {why} is the cause (a dc_why_* message or the system's text).
cmd_misc_dc_probe_failed_fix: Fix of the new-terminal check when the probe failed. The command stays as typed.
cmd_misc_dc_unknown_error: Shown in place of the cause when the login-shell probe failed with no message.
cmd_misc_dc_unknown_version: Shown as the version of an installed desktop app whose version could not be read: `<path> is an unknown version, the CLI is 1.5.0`.
cmd_misc_dc_why_hostd_silent: Cause of a silent hostd: the handshake timed out.
cmd_misc_dc_why_probe_not_run: Cause shown when the probe thread failed to run.
cmd_misc_dc_why_shell_no_path: Cause of a failed probe: the shell answered without a PATH.
cmd_misc_dc_why_shell_silent: Cause of a failed probe: the login shell took too long.
cmd_misc_dc_why_start_failed: Cause of a failed probe: the login shell could not be started.

cmd_misc_dc_why_windows.description: Cause of a skipped probe: a new terminal on Windows reads the registry's Path, not a shell rc.

cmd_misc_dev_runner_already: Output of `atlas dev --detach` when a runner already owns the project. The two commands stay as typed.
cmd_misc_dev_runner_started: Output of `atlas dev --detach` once the background runner answers. The two commands stay as typed.
cmd_misc_doctor_dir_row: Row of an Atlas temp or cache folder: its size against its cap.
cmd_misc_doctor_dir_row_orphaned: Same as doctor_dir_row for a folder whose owner process has ended.
cmd_misc_doctor_dirs_heading: Heading of the list of folders Atlas created, with size against cap, in `atlas doctor --hygiene`.
cmd_misc_doctor_disk_heading: Heading of the per-project disk list of `atlas doctor --hygiene`.
cmd_misc_doctor_dry_run: First sentence of the dry-run summary of `atlas doctor --hygiene`; {count} is the orphan count, {size} what a fix would free.
cmd_misc_doctor_dry_run_marker: Second sentence of the dry-run summary, only when Spotlight indexes folders Atlas owns.
cmd_misc_doctor_dry_run_yours: Last sentence of the dry-run summary: Atlas never deletes build output, dependencies or worktrees.
cmd_misc_doctor_env_unreadable: Three indented lines under the orphan list of `atlas doctor --hygiene` on systems where the environment of other processes cannot be read (macOS, Windows).
cmd_misc_doctor_fixed: First sentence of the result of `atlas doctor --hygiene --fix`.
cmd_misc_doctor_fixed_marked: Second sentence of the result of `--fix`, only when markers were added.

cmd_misc_doctor_indexed_heading.description: Heading of the folders Spotlight indexes in `atlas doctor --hygiene`; a macOS-only section, one folder per line below.

cmd_misc_doctor_no_projects: Under the disk heading of `atlas doctor --hygiene` when the app knows no project.
cmd_misc_doctor_orphans: First line of `atlas doctor --hygiene`: the processes Atlas tagged whose owner is gone, and how many belong to live sessions (left alone).
cmd_misc_doctor_survivors: Last line of the result of `--fix` (exit 1) when some orphan did not die; {pids} is the list of pids.
cmd_misc_down_not_running: Output of `atlas down` when there is no runner for the project (nothing to do, exit 0).
cmd_misc_down_stopped: Output of `atlas down` once the runner and its services ended.
cmd_misc_down_timeout: Error of `atlas down` (exit 1) when the runner did not end in time; the command stays as typed.
cmd_misc_heavy_ctx_join: Context of `atlas run --heavy` when the queue folder cannot be used.
cmd_misc_heavy_ctx_spawn: Context of `atlas run`: the program could not be started; {command} is the command line.
cmd_misc_heavy_got_slot: Line on stderr of `atlas run --heavy` after a wait; {wait} is a compact duration such as 1m05s.
cmd_misc_heavy_hold_anyway: Line on stderr of `atlas run --heavy` when the load or memory gate did not clear in time; {why} is a heavy_hold_* message.
cmd_misc_heavy_hold_load: Why a heavy job waits: the 5-minute load average is at or above the limit. {load} and {max} are numbers with one decimal.
cmd_misc_heavy_hold_memory: Why a heavy job waits: free memory is under the minimum percentage.
cmd_misc_heavy_hold_waiting: Line on stderr of `atlas run --heavy` while the load or memory gate holds the job; said once per reason; {why} is a heavy_hold_* message.
cmd_misc_heavy_interrupted_gates: Line on stderr of `atlas run --heavy` when Ctrl-C ended the wait for load or memory (exit 130).
cmd_misc_heavy_interrupted_queued: Line on stderr of `atlas run --heavy` when Ctrl-C ended the wait for a slot (exit 130).
cmd_misc_heavy_queued: First line of the wait notice of `atlas run --heavy`: {ahead} is the number of jobs in front of it.
cmd_misc_heavy_queued_eta: Same as heavy_queued when past runs give an estimate; {eta} is a compact duration.
cmd_misc_heavy_row_running: What a running job shows in `atlas heavy status`: its age and the estimate from past runs (? when unknown).
cmd_misc_heavy_row_waiting: What a queued job shows in `atlas heavy status`: how long it waits and the estimate (? when unknown).
cmd_misc_heavy_running_row: Row of the wait notice of `atlas run --heavy`: a job that holds a slot, with its age.
cmd_misc_heavy_status_busy: First part of the header of `atlas heavy status`: running jobs against the number of slots. The parts are joined by commas.
cmd_misc_heavy_status_load: Optional part of the header of `atlas heavy status`: the 5-minute load average, one decimal.
cmd_misc_heavy_status_memory: Optional part of the header of `atlas heavy status`: free memory.
cmd_misc_heavy_status_waiting: Second part of the header of `atlas heavy status`: queued jobs.
cmd_misc_init_created: Output of `atlas init`, after a green ✓.
cmd_misc_init_detected: Output of `atlas init`: the language (and framework) found in the folder, e.g. `rust (axum)`.
cmd_misc_init_exists: Error of `atlas init` when the folder already has an atlas.yaml. Lowercase: the CLI puts `error:` before it.
cmd_misc_init_no_services: Output of `atlas init` when no service could be inferred.
cmd_misc_init_services: Output of `atlas init`: the service names written to atlas.yaml, comma separated.
cmd_misc_mcp_not_dir: Error of `atlas mcp --dir`. Lowercase: the CLI puts `error:` before it.
cmd_misc_release_checksum_mismatch: Error of `atlas update` and `atlas desktop`: the downloaded file does not match its sha256. Lowercase: the CLI puts `error:` before it.
cmd_misc_release_ctx_missing_asset: Context of a failed download of a release file (the archive or its .sha256) in `atlas update` and `atlas desktop`.
cmd_misc_release_no_checksum: Error of `atlas update` and `atlas desktop`: the checksum file is missing, so nothing is installed. Lowercase: the CLI puts `error:` before it.
cmd_misc_run_cache_ctx_key: Context of `atlas run --cache` when an output path is bad or a declared tool cannot report its version.
cmd_misc_run_cache_hit: Line on stderr of `atlas run --cache` when a stored result was restored instead of running the command; {key} is 12 characters, {count} the restored files.
cmd_misc_run_cache_not_stored_failed: Line on stderr of `atlas run --cache`: only an exit code 0 is stored unless --cache-failures is set.
cmd_misc_run_cache_not_stored_too_big: Line on stderr of `atlas run --cache`: the entry alone is larger than the whole cache cap.
cmd_misc_run_cache_store_failed: Line on stderr of `atlas run --cache`: the cache could not write; the command's own result is returned anyway.
cmd_misc_run_cache_stored: Line on stderr of `atlas run --cache` after a miss whose result was stored.
cmd_misc_run_cache_unusable: Line on stderr of `atlas run --cache` when a stored entry is damaged: the command runs for real and overwrites it.
